Front: The five Vs of big data
Back: Volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value.

Front: Veracity — an example from our starter file
Back: Madrid typed as “Madrid”, “MADRID” and “madrid”: the data cannot be trusted as it is.
Up: a bigger machine. Out: more machines working together in a cluster.
Map (records → key–value pairs), shuffle (same key → same machine), reduce (combine the values of each key).
OLTP runs the business with many short operations on few rows; OLAP analyses it with long queries over many rows and few columns.
Row-oriented keeps the values of one row together (CSV); columnar keeps the values of one column together (Parquet).

Front: What is inside a Parquet file?
Back: Row groups, each made of one column chunk per column, and a footer with the schema and statistics (min, max, nulls).
It read one column, read fewer (compressed) bytes, parsed no text, and skipped row groups using statistics.
A transformation (filter, select) only extends the plan; an action (count, write) makes Spark compute.
Data that fits on one machine: DuckDB. Data or work too big for one machine, or shared by many teams: Spark.
A ledger is an ordered record of transactions; append-only means records are only added at the end, never changed.
A 256-bit value, written as 64 hexadecimal characters, always the same length whatever the input.
A tiny change in the input (Madrid → madrid) gives a completely different hash.

Front: Why does a change in block 3 break block 4?
Back: Block 4 stores the hash of block 3; a changed block 3 has a new hash, so block 4's stored value no longer matches.
The data can still be changed, but the change cannot be hidden from someone who checks the chain.
The procedure by which the nodes of a blockchain agree on the next block.

Front: Proof of work in one idea
Back: Find a nonce that gives the block's hash a required number of leading zeros: hard to find, easy to check.

Front: Proof of stake in one idea
Back: Validators lock a deposit (stake); they are chosen to propose blocks and lose part of the stake if they cheat.
Permissionless: anyone may write (Bitcoin). Permissioned: only approved organizations write (Hyperledger Fabric).
A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically, the same way on every node, when its condition is met.
